Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-07-15 | AMZN | Overweight | -4.0% | -3.0% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN stays an Overweight, but the trader's execution — 40% of the add at $254.96, a close above the plan's own prohibited upper Bollinger Band ($254.80) — is corrected to a staged, smaller build. Seed only ~10–15% of the incremental add now (or on an intraday dip back inside the band), add 25–30% into the $247–253 10-EMA/50-SMA confluence, and hold the final 25–30% for a volume-confirmed breakout (two closes above $256.48 on >40M shares) with the 50-SMA slope flattening. Target ~1.0x standard weight now with a path to 1.25x, hard-cap ~1.25x into the Q2 print and carry no more than 50–60% of the target overweight into it. Structural stop $237.50 (below the $238 base low / $238.81 VWMA); cut the add back to standard on a decisive loss of $241.38; no leverage; size inversely to the $7.48 ATR (~2.9% of price). Horizon 3–6 months, first target $264–266, secondary $278.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is not the hard part; the entry is, and both sides largely agree on that. The bull wins the business case outright and the conservative analyst never actually contests it: Q1 FY2026 revenue +16.6% to $181.5B, gross margin +124bp to 51.8%, operating margin +132bp to 13.1%, operating income +29.6% to $23.9B, Q1 operating cash flow $26.0B (+53% YoY), core EPS ~$1.92 (+21% YoY) even after conceding the $12.3B non-cash mark-up, a negative cash-conversion cycle (~−54 days, inventory down $1.8B while revenue grew 16.6%) and $25.3B of deferred revenue. The conservative analyst's "negative FCF = mandate breach" framing does not survive contact with the balance sheet he himself cites: $144B of cash and securities against $122.6B of debt, $800M/quarter of interest expense against $23.9B/quarter of operating income, and net obligations including leases near 0.45–0.50x EBITDA. That is a duration-and-ROI question, not a solvency one, and it rules out Sell and Underweight. It also matches the 2026-07-08 lesson, where refusing any starter at $243.62 while price sat above a rising 200-SMA cost ~3.4 points of alpha in five days.

The conservative analyst wins two points decisively and the neutral analyst converts both into the right fix. First, the plan's no-add-above-$254.80 rule versus a $254.96 Tranche 1 is a genuine internal contradiction — if the rule is real the first tranche cannot be 40% at market, and if it is not real the "mechanistically cautious" language is marketing. Second, the payoff on new money at spot is poor: $17.46 down to the $237.50 stop against first resistance at the $256.48 session high, then $264–266, then $278.56 — a ladder, not a clean 3:1. The aggressive analyst reaches "better than 3-to-1" only by leaning on the $313 sell-side marker that the conservative correctly identifies as a low-information summary with no price target detail, in a data set that admittedly contains no valuation multiples, no Q2 guidance or consensus, and no quantified AI-capex returns. The aggressive case is also wrong on tape conviction: one close marginally above the upper band, one day above a 50-SMA that is still declining ($253.10, from $257.10 on 6/18), is a reclaim awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed regime shift — and with ATR at $7.48 a single ordinary down day lands near $247.

The neutral analyst's synthesis is the strongest argument on the table and it is what I am adopting. It keeps the constructive bias the Research Manager's Overweight plan requires (200-SMA at $233.79 rising, price +9.1% above it, fresh MACD zero-line cross at +$0.26 vs signal −$1.86 and histogram +$2.12, RSI 60.14 with headroom, 45.2M shares vs a 30–40M norm, and a resolution of the multi-week $238–248 base) while refusing to pay the extended upper-band print for it. Concretely: a 10–15% starter rather than 40%; the preferred tranche into the $247–253 zone where the 10-EMA ($246.40) and reclaimed 50-SMA ($253.10) sit and the $237.50 stop is defensible; the final tranche only on a volume-confirmed breakout above $256.48; and — the neutral's sharpest point, which the aggressive analyst ignored — the $241.38 de-risking trigger sits exactly where a perfectly healthy breakout-and-backtest lands, so entries closer to $247–253 are what make that rule a feature rather than a shake-out mechanism.

Where I side with the conservative analyst against both others is the Q2 print. The earnings-quality flags are real and specific, not rhetorical: OCF of $26.0B trailing net income of $30.3B with deferred tax expense jumping to $12.8B from $507M; other non-current assets up $29.2B in a quarter (the AI equity stakes); the $12.3B mark-up is symmetric and can reverse into a distorted comparison base where consensus is split. The bear's structural points compound it — TTM FCF of ~−$2.5B against $151B trailing capex, capex/D&A at 2.14x guaranteeing a multi-year depreciation drag, debt from $68.8B to $122.6B in one quarter with $53.4B of LT issuance and a $25B bond pending, funding mix shifting from internal cash to the debt market, and $569.3B of contractual purchase obligations ($57.1B due within twelve months) — which is precisely why the 70% pre-print carry is too high and 50–60% is right. The news flow supports no stronger a stance: 20 of 183 records, all July 14, with a six-day July 8–13 gap; Jefferies is a summary with no estimates; Wells Fargo's $312→$313 is immaterial; the NY data-center moratorium with fourteen states considering similar moves is a genuine medium-term regulatory-diffusion risk but, as the conservative concedes, no AMZN site was named and it is not a July 15 catalyst.

Net: business quality and trend earn the Overweight; entry mechanics, absent valuation support, and the marks/print risk earn the staging, the reduced size and the lower pre-print cap. What would move this to Buy: a clean backtest that holds $247–253 with the 50-SMA slope flattening, or a volume-confirmed breakout above $256.48, ideally with actual valuation multiples and Q2 consensus in hand. What would move it to Hold or below: a decisive loss of $241.38 that then breaks $238/$237.50, or Q2 evidence of a widening FCF deficit, a further debt step-up, a mark-up reversal producing an optical EPS decline, or a demanding multiple surfacing on a cash-negative core. Explicit gaps carried forward: no P/E or EV/EBITDA on GAAP or core, no Q2 guidance or consensus bar, no quantified return on the $177B/yr capex program, no social-sentiment data — any of those should trigger a re-size.

**Price Target**: 265.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of −3.0% (raw −4.0% vs SPY) went against the call, but five days is far too short to judge a 3–6 month Overweight thesis — it does, however, confirm the entry-mechanics critique was right: the market never validated paying up near $254.96 and instead gave back roughly a full ATR-plus. That supports the neutral analyst's staging and stop discipline (the $247–253 tranche and $237.50 structural stop now look well-placed) and undercuts nothing in the business case, while validating the concern that the "breakout" was a reclaim awaiting confirmation, not a regime shift. Lesson for next time: when price closes above a plan's own prohibited band the same day, treat that as a timing signal for a lower entry rather than a reason to size up, and weight the 5-day tape confirmation explicitly against the stated 3–6 month horizon before assigning an Overweight.

[2026-07-14 | AMZN | Overweight | +0.0% | +0.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Build AMZN toward an overweight, but do not pay up at $247.49 into the $252.97 upper-band / $253.37 falling 50-SMA confluence (~2% upside to resistance vs. a demonstrated 17% drawdown template). Deploy Tranche 1 (≈1/3) on a limit near $241 (Bollinger mid-band $240.93, add room toward the $237.9 VWMA / $236–237 shelf) and hold total pre-confirmation exposure near market weight (~1.0x); Tranche 2 only on a daily close above $253.50 on ≥50M shares with MACD back above zero, which earns the full 1.2–1.3x overweight band; Tranche 3 reserved for a Q2 print confirming FCF stabilization and margin hold. Use a closing-basis failure of the rising 200-SMA ($233.60) to shrink the trade add, high-volume break of $227.01/$225.55 as hard invalidation (cut the trade-sized add, not the core), and size each tranche so a $7.36 ATR day is tolerable. Horizon 6–12 months.

**Investment Thesis**: The strategic question is settled by evidence neither the bear nor the neutral analyst rebutted: Q1 2026 revenue +16.6% YoY to $181.5B, operating income +29.6% to $23.9B, operating margin +130bps to 13.1%, record TTM OCF of $148.5B, ~$144B cash and securities against ~$123B long-term debt on ~$437B equity, a P/E near a multi-year low, and price 5.9% above a *rising* 200-SMA at $233.60. The aggressive analyst is right that capex is the seed of future cash flow rather than proof of value destruction, and the conservative analyst's case never crosses into solvency — $800M of quarterly interest against $23.9B of quarterly operating income is ~25–30x coverage. That rules out Sell, and it also means a market-weight-or-below stance cannot be the terminal position, which is where I overrule the conservative analyst.

The bear and neutral analysts win the mechanics and the quality-of-earnings argument, and those win the sizing, not the direction. (1) Unrefuted cash-flow fact: FY2025 FCF fell ~77% YoY and Q1 2026 FCF was roughly −$18.2B as Q1 capex of $44.2B annualizes toward ~$177B; the aggressive analyst led with gross OCF and never answered the net number. (2) The "rounding error" leverage defense fails as a trend statement: long-term debt went $68.8B to $122.6B in a single quarter with interest expense +48% YoY. (3) Earnings quality was conceded by the bull: ~$12.3B of the $2.78 EPS is a non-cash equity revaluation (clean ≈$2.00), and a low multiple on inflated GAAP EPS is a weak valuation floor. (4) The sharpest forward point went unanswered — today's 13.1% margin does not yet carry depreciation on data centers still being built, so part of the celebrated ROI is front-loaded operating leverage ahead of a margin squeeze. (5) Tactically the bear has the better of it: price under a *falling* 50-SMA at $253.37, MACD −0.654 below zero, a July bounce on light 30–40M share volume the bull conceded, a Bollinger squeeze that can resolve either way, and a lower band at $228.89.

The neutral analyst beats both extremes and is the tie-breaker on implementation. His arithmetic correction is right — from $241 to first resistance at ~$253 is ~12 points against ~8.5 points to a $232.50 stop, about 1.4:1, and only 3:1 if the $253 breakout and the run to $274–278 actually print; underwriting the second leg before the first resistance is reclaimed is paying for an unproven outcome. He is also right that $232.50 is ~1.15 ATR from a $241 entry; the fix is not widening into a 3–4 ATR hole but keeping Tranche 1 near one-third of target, treating a *closing* break of $233.60 as the tactical warning, and reserving hard invalidation for a high-volume break of $227.01/$225.55. His 50M-share threshold objectively replaces the trader's undefined "volume-confirmed" and is the line between a 30–40M drift and institutional demand. Prior AMZN work supports exactly this structure: the 07-07 Hold correctly refused to add 5 points under resistance and produced no signal, while the 07-06 and 06-30 Overweights earned small positive alpha from staged pullback-limited starters rather than spot purchases — and the 07-07 GOOGL miss confirms unconfirmed entries ahead of a 50-SMA reclaim underperform.

What would change the call: two consecutive daily closes above $253.50 on ≥50M shares with MACD >0 converts this to full Buy and authorizes the 1.2–1.3x band; a MACD zero-line cross plus a reclaimed 50-SMA reinforces it. A closing break of $233.60 takes the trade add to zero and the position toward market weight; a high-volume break of $227.01/$225.55 makes it Underweight with the February $196–199 air pocket as strategic reference. On fundamentals, Q2 evidence of FCF turning positive with margins holding strengthens the overweight, while a sustained negative FCF run-rate, long-term debt climbing well beyond $122.6B with a steepening interest trend, or a reversal of the equity-stake revaluation dragging reported EPS moves it to Underweight. Evidence gaps stated explicitly: no Q2 earnings date or data in this window, no tool-confirmed proof of realized AI-capex ROI, no sentiment report, a thin single-day news tape, and debt figures that have varied across sources — hence triggers are technical and balance-sheet based rather than assumption-based.

**Price Target**: 270.0

**Time Horizon**: 6-12 months

REFLECTION:
Five days produced +0.5% alpha on a 0.0% raw return — directionally a coin flip, and far too short a window to test a 6–12 month overweight thesis. What it does support is the implementation: refusing to pay $247.49 into the $253 confluence was harmless because no breakout printed, so the staged-limit structure cost nothing while the FCF/capex debate remains entirely unresolved. Lesson for next time: on a multi-month call, record at the outset which specific trigger levels (the $241 limit, the $253.50/50M-share confirmation) would actually have fired, so a flat five-day tape can be scored as "no signal" rather than silently credited to the thesis.

[2026-07-13 | AMZN | Underweight | +1.1% | +2.0% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN: trim existing exposure to roughly 0.65x–0.75x of a standard benchmark allocation (a 25%–35% cut of intended weight), and do not initiate at $247.31 with price jammed under the $252–$254 confluence (falling 50-SMA $253.72, upper Bollinger $252.16) while MACD sits at −1.05, still below zero. Treat $252–$254 as a trimming/reassessment zone and re-entry trigger — not the "stop loss" the trader mislabeled, since a stop above spot is meaningless on a trim — and use a daily close below the rising 200-SMA at $233.47 as the hard trend-risk control that cuts AMZN to minimal or zero. Size so the $247.31-to-$233.47 distance (~$13.8, ~1.8x ATR of $7.56) fits the pre-set portfolio risk budget, and rebuild toward benchmark weight only on a decisive close above $252–$254 on above-average volume, or on a stabilized pullback into $237–$233.50 with Q2 evidence that capex is no longer consuming all operating cash flow. Horizon 3–6 months.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk analysts converged on the direction — reduce, do not add — and the disagreement was only about degree, which is exactly the dispute this decision has to settle.

**What the bear side won decisively.** The tactical setup is unambiguous: AMZN closed at $247.31, below the falling 50-SMA at $253.72 and capped by the $252–$254 confluence where that 50-SMA meets the upper Bollinger band at $252.16; MACD has crossed its signal line but remains at −1.05, below zero; RSI at 52.9 is neutral, not a breakout reading. That is a repaired bounce, not a trend reassertion, and the aggressive analyst's point stands that waiting for confirmation above the zone means absorbing the full $13.8 (~1.8x ATR) distance down to the 200-SMA before the long-term trend even breaks. The fundamental overlay is equally specific: TTM free cash flow slightly negative (FY2025 FCF ~$7.7B, TTM ~−$2.5B), capex roughly 102% of operating cash flow (Q1 capex $44.2B against $26.0B OCF), long-term debt more than doubled to $122.6B with $53.4B issued in a single quarter and interest expense up 48%, operating leases of $91.6B, contractual obligations near $569B, and capex incurred but not paid at $27.0B. Q1 EPS of $2.78 was flattered by a $15.6B non-operating gain including a $12.3B non-cash revaluation — clean EPS is closer to ~$2.00, against a harsh YoY comp. That combination — paying up under resistance for a debt-funded capex cycle with no demonstrated return above cost of capital on a $151B TTM capex base — is what makes this a reduce, not a hold.

**What the bull side won, and why this is Underweight rather than Sell.** The conservative analyst is right that the primary trend is intact: price is above the rising 200-SMA at $233.47, the 50>200 golden cross is preserved, revenue grew 16.6% to $181.5B, operating income grew 29.6% to $23.85B with 130bps of margin expansion to 13.1%, TTM operating cash flow is $148.5B and liquidity is ~$144B. The aggressive analyst's framing of that as "static trend worship" overreaches — those are long-term trend facts, not near-term entry signals, but they do rule out exiting a franchise whose operating income is compounding at ~2x revenue. Equally, the trader's own "Sell" proposal is really a sizing call (trim to 0.5x–0.75x), not a risk-off exit. Underweight captures that precisely: reduce exposure, keep a core, take the optionality off the table, but do not abandon the position at a level still above a rising 200-SMA.

**Where I moderate both extremes.** I side with the conservative and neutral analysts against the aggressive analyst on the $25B data-center headline: it is a headline and a summary with no disclosed structure, pricing, or market reaction, against ~$144B of cash and securities — treating it as a near-certain bearish catalyst is a sentiment bet, not a risk read, and it should not drive size. Likewise the late-June 248M-share session could be accumulation rather than a dead-cat bounce, so I do not trim at the maximum 50% end of the range absent evidence the caller is tactically overweight. Conversely, I side with the neutral and aggressive analysts against the conservative analyst on sizing: a token 25% trim is too light when the caller may already be at or above benchmark, and the neutral resolution — trim 25%–35%, toward 0.65x–0.75x, with up to 50% only if tactically overweight — is the right calibration for an unknown book. I also adopt the neutral analyst's correction that a bare touch of $233.47 is not a buy signal; support must stabilize.

**Two process corrections.** First, the trader's stop at $254 is not a stop — it sits above spot. On a trim, $252–$254 is an upside invalidation and re-entry trigger; the real risk line is a daily close below $233.47. Second, prior AMZN work cut starters too small on short-window bounce objections (the 2026-07-06 Overweight earned +1.6% five-day alpha and the reflection rightly noted the entry-timing discount, not the thesis, was the marginal variable) — the reverse discipline applies here: the five-day alpha does not validate a FCF/leverage thesis, and the GOOGL lesson that "rebound, not trend-change" setups deserve zero positive momentum weight until a volume-backed close above the 50-SMA prints argues for trimming now rather than waiting for a $233–$237 retest.
